name: Strike
description: A basic physical blow. No resource cost.

name: Guard Stance
description: Brace. Sharply raises defense but only briefly.

name: Rush Barrage
description: A dense flurry of close-range strikes.

name: Tempo Halt
description: Freezes the flow of the battle for every opponent.

name: Restore
description: Reverts an ally's wounds. Enough to buy a turn, not enough to undo one.

name: Emerald Snare
description: Ranged binding attack that slows the target. Power 75 sits below the free basic attack, so for Kakyoin's atk 78 this trades damage away for the slow rather than adding one to the other; see the riposte note and the issue it points at.

name: Emerald Splash
description: Scatters a burst of psychic emeralds across the enemy line.

name: Blade Volley
description: Scatters throwing blades across the enemy line. Thrown by the handful, into a moment that is not moving.

name: Sun Flare
description: A searing burst of heat that leaves the target bleeding heat.

name: Concussive Slam
description: A heavy blow that can stagger the target outright.

name: Riposte
description: Answers the blow before it lands. The cut is shallow; the habit it breaks is not. Power shipped at 85 and measured at 0 wins in 300: because damage subtracts half the target's defence, any power below the basic attack's 100 is a downgrade the AI's scorer cannot see, since it prices the debuff separately and generously. 110 is the least that makes a paid skill worth more than the free one it displaces.

name: Flurry Cut
description: Two shallow cuts in the time one blow would take. Power is 105 and not lower on purpose: damage subtracts half the target's defence, so anything under the free attack's 100 is a downgrade, which is the fault riposte shipped with and #33 records. The point of the skill is tempo_cost 700 against the basic attack's 1000 - the first content here that uses tempo as a design lever rather than copying the default. Note that the scorer has no term for tempo_cost, so the AI cannot see the property this skill exists for.

name: Wither Hex
description: Lays a weakening mark on every opponent at once. The first skill in this file that deals no damage of any kind, which is the point and also the risk: the harness counts a combatant inert when it deals no damage and heals nothing, so its carrier has to hold skill.strike too or a debuffer doing its job perfectly would be reported as having sat out the batch. Potency is 26 and not 40 because damage subtracts half the target's defence after multiplying by attack, so an attack debuff bites harder than its percentage: at 40 it would halve Kakyoin's output rather than trim it. Same asymmetry as the riposte note, seen from the other side. Duration shipped at 3 and the encounter measured 92% against a band of 58..86, which is the whole story of this skill: the Weaver managed 2.70 actions per battle and 1.73 casts before dying with alive% 0%, so the party's output fell 7% where 24% was intended, and a fight that was supposed to lengthen instead came in at 20 turns, shorter than both its sibling fixtures. Duration is now 8. That is long against everything else in this file, and it is long on purpose, because uptime here is not bounded by how often the hex is cast but by how briefly its caster lives - the mark has to outlive the one who laid it. The scorer follows along without any special case: status_points for AtkDown is baseline * potency / 100 * duration, so 100 * 26/100 * 8 = 208, doubled for two targets and taken at the 85% chance to land gives 354 against a free strike's 100. That margin should change nothing about how often the skill is used, because the measured 64% share is AGGRESSIVE_SKILL_CHANCE 65 and not the score. When only one party member is still standing the target count halves the score, and the carrier goes back to hitting things, which is correct behaviour that no branch anywhere asks for. One thing this skill proved about the engine rather than about itself: the Weaver's accuracy rolls came to 295 against 295 strike uses, exactly equal, so a status-only skill draws no accuracy roll at all.
